Player 2's Boardwalk with three houses now costs $1400. Park Place with two houses costs $500.

Selling two houses from each pink property would raise cash to $102. That leaves one house on every property, dropping the rent spike to about $50 per space. Indiana is a $90 hit that would leave a $38 shortfall. Community Chest and Chance cards could also cause trouble.

I am deciding optional actions after landing. I will not sell houses preemptively because Player 4 is about to roll from Jail into the pink properties. I am also verifying whether this is my turn 85 post-roll.

Player 4 cannot use Connecticut or the B&O Railroad to build anything useful. St. James Place would not complete an orange set for them either. The only remaining trade chip is Pennsylvania Avenue. Player 4 previously rejected a $250 offer for it. Even with $529 they might still refuse because buying it mortgaged would cost roughly $376 in unmortgage and Pacific Avenue.

Player 4 cannot complete the green set this lap even if they buy Pennsylvania Avenue from me. The total cost is $726, but they only have $529. Selling it for $100 would still leave them with a mortgaged property and no cash to unmortgage it. I will not re-propose the trade because Player 4 already rejected it twice.

Player 2 cannot help me survive the upcoming reds. I have no New York to complete an orange set with them, and they have no reason to pay me cash for a property I cannot use.

From Tennessee Avenue, the next spaces are New York, Free Parking, Kentucky, and Chance. New York costs $16, which I can afford. Kentucky costs $250, which I cannot afford.

From Tennessee Avenue, the next spaces are Indiana, Illinois, Atlantic, Ventnor, Marvin Gardens, NC, and PA. Indiana costs $90, which I can barely afford. Illinois costs $250, which I cannot pay. Atlantic costs $22, which I can cover. Ventnor and NC cost $22 and $26, which I can pay. PA is mine. The Short Line costs $100, which I am short by $48. Water Works is mortgaged and costs nothing. I will not land on B&O, Pacific, Community Chest, or Chance from this roll.

Roll 12 to Go to Jail is the only safe landing from Tennessee Avenue. The other dangerous rolls are 3, 5, and 6 for Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Roll 4 on Chance could also be bad.

Player 4 has an eight-in-thirty-six chance of landing on a pink property from Jail. If they do, I would collect $450 to $500 in rent and keep my houses. That would give me enough cash to survive the upcoming red properties without selling anything.

I will not sell houses now. I will keep the pink trap for Player 4 and only sell if I hit reds later. I am also weighing whether to offer Player 4 Pennsylvania Avenue for $200 instead of $250. They may prefer cash to pay the upcoming pink rent rather than spend it on a property.

Player 4 cannot afford the pink rent even after buying Pennsylvania Avenue for $200. They would still lack enough cash to pay the $450 to $500 rent, so they would mortgage properties instead. They prefer keeping liquidity rather than spending it on a property that would not solve their immediate cash shortage.

Player 2 cannot pay enough to survive the upcoming reds. Even with all their cash, they still fall short of the $250 rent on Kentucky and Illinois. Player 4 can provide enough cash, but only if I give up Pennsylvania Avenue.

Player 4 might accept Pennsylvania Avenue for $300. That would leave them with $229, which is too little to buy Pacific Avenue. I would gain $352 in cash and survive the upcoming reds without selling any houses.

Player 4 will reject the $300 offer for Pennsylvania Avenue again. Their earlier objection was specifically about needing cash to pay pink rent while Pacific Avenue remains in the bank and they are positioned right in front of the pinks. Both conditions remain true now.
